newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end mostly higher.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mostly higher as continued local short covering lifted futures to or near best levels of the day late, traders said.
Early pressure lacked followthrough and prices drifted higher in very thin post holiday trade. Outside interest was very light, especially with Canadian markets closed for Boxing Day, traders said.

Cash trade in the U.S. provided little direction as mills were asking $400 per cwt and retailers were reportedly only bidding $375 as poor weather conditions cut demand over much of the country, cash sources said.

However, expectations that demand for wood would increase after the holidays kept the market supported. Cash markets usually rise in the first part of the new year as demand builds into the spring building season, traders said.
Lumber closed up $3.90 per tbf to off $1.00 with January up most at $402.70 and March up $0.50 at $391.70 per tbf.
